title: LLM Pretraining with Continuous Concepts
claim: A two-stage procedure first extracts and selects concepts from a pretrained model, then predicts them and interleaves them into hidden states.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, stacked token blocks with arrows and inset bar charts
description: Two rounded gray panels show the method. The left panel, 'Extracting concepts from a pretrained SAE model's hidden state', has a stack of tokens A B C feeding a block h_con. Yellow hidden-state cells sit above it, then f_con and output tokens B C D. A dash-dot gradient-flow line marks attribution, with the formula ∇_concept −log p('D'|'ABC'). A trapezoid SAE encoder and an orange bar chart of 'Selected Concepts' I sit to the right. The right panel, 'Learning to predict concepts & mixing/interleaving continuous concepts into the hidden state', shows a similar stack with blocks h and f. Green concept cells alternate with yellow token cells. A green bar chart of predicted concepts z, a 'min CE(orange, green)' loss, and a compressed 'Continuous concept' ĉ feed back into the stream. Yellow, green, orange and blue color-code the elements.
caption: Overview of \sname. We use an SAE to extract concepts from a pretrained model's hidden state $h_\mathtt{con}$ and then select important concepts based on the attribution score (i.e., measuring the influence on the output). These selected concepts are used as labels $\mathcal{I}$ for concept prediction by minimizing the cross-entropy loss $\mathrm{CE}(\cdot,\cdot)$. The predicted concepts $\rvz$ are then compressed into a compact vector, forming a continuous concept $\rvc$, which is mixed into the model’s hidden state by interleaving with token hidden representations. We demonstrate that \sname is more sample efficient and outperforms standard next-token prediction and knowledge distillation baselines.
abstract: Next token prediction has been the standard training objective used in large language model pretraining. Representations are learned as a result of optimizing for token-level perplexity. We propose Continuous Concept Mixing (CoCoMix), a novel pretraining framework that combines discrete next token prediction with continuous concepts. Specifically, CoCoMix predicts continuous concepts learned from a pretrained sparse autoencoder and mixes them into the model's hidden state by interleaving with token hidden representations. Through experiments on multiple benchmarks, including language modeling and downstream reasoning tasks, we show that CoCoMix is more sample efficient and consistently outperforms standard next token prediction, knowledge distillation and inserting pause tokens. We find that combining both concept learning and interleaving in an end-to-end framework is critical to performance gains. Furthermore, CoCoMix enhances interpretability and steerability by allowing direct inspection and modification of the predicted concept, offering a transparent way to guide the model's internal reasoning process.
